# `acmedns` — specification

## Maturity

**Grade:** 2 · S2 E1 A1 H1 P– · limited by scope (parity) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** parity — lego v5 `challenge/dns01` + its generic providers (`rfc2136`, `acmedns`, `httpreq`, `exec`), certmagic `DNS01Solver` (surveyed 2026-10-16 within acme's full-competitor survey, items R12/R13; vendor providers excluded by the owner)

**Audit:** review 2026-10-16 · mutation 2026-11-25 (185/196, 11 eq) · src 50bccc1cde21e9b0

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-10-16 (ACMEDNS_FUZZ: acme-dns `/register` reply, TXT reply through `txtPresent`; 500 seeds per test run, every reach label hit) · ct n/a — holds no secret computation: TSIG is `dns.tsig`'s (burned, stack-probed), credentials are passed through to `http` headers · panic 2026-11-14 (sweep of every pub entry point: HIGH `post`/`register` read the response body with no time bound after the head, so a server sending `200` + `Content-Length` and stalling blocked the caller forever, now `readAllAllocTimeout(64 KiB, total_timeout_ms)`; MED `propagation_timeout_ms` was checked only between passes, while one pass could run servers × addresses × `query_timeout_ms`, now gated before every query; MED a failing `toOwnedSlice` in `zone.nameservers` was a use-after-free and double free instead of `error.OutOfMemory`, plus two leaks on allocation failure; LOW basic-auth bound comment 379 -> 378)

**Performance:** n/a — every step waits on DNS, an HTTP endpoint, a child process or the CA

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** no

## Compared with

What a DNS-01 user of the field's main clients gets, from their documentation (2026-10-16; no
source read). The vendor-API providers (lego has 200+, libdns several dozen) are deliberately not
here: the owner chose the generic ones (acme survey 2026-10-16, Q2).

**Where we are ahead:** the only Zig implementation; propagation is checked against the
authoritative servers by default and, with `check_resolvers`, against the recursive ones too.
**Where we are behind:** no vendor APIs (by decision) and no GSS-TSIG for Windows "secure only" zones (`dns.tsig`
is HMAC only), both in *What is deliberately not done*.

## Design & invariants

- **Flow (`Dns01Solver.present`):** value = base64url(SHA-256(key authorization)) via
  `acme.jws`; name = `override_name` or `_acme-challenge.<domain>`; CNAME walk (one hop per query,
  `max_cname_hops` = 8, a loop is `CnameLoop`); zone = `Options.zone` or the longest suffix whose
  own SOA is in an answer section (NXDOMAIN, NODATA and CNAME move to the parent; the root is never
  a candidate); a challenge name outside `Options.zone` is refused (`ZoneNotFound`) before anything is
  published; publish; wait. A SERVFAIL or REFUSED on the CNAME or SOA question is `error.ResolverFailed`
  ("could not find out"), never read as "no CNAME" / "no SOA here", which would publish at the
  undelegated name or in the parent zone. The record handed to the publisher carries the effective name and
  the zone, plus token and key authorization for the RAW modes.
- **Cleanup is exact:** every published record is kept (heap-stable, so its slices survive list
  growth) until `cleanup(domain, value)` finds it; the list has room reserved BEFORE publishing, so
  a published record can never be forgotten for want of memory. A publisher that fails and a wait that
  fails both clean up themselves (best effort: the update may have landed before the failure showed;
  publishers treat removing an absent record as a no-op), because `acme.Client` calls cleanup only
  after a successful present. The same (domain, value) presented twice is one record with a reference
  count (the second `present` publishes and waits for nothing); the DNS value is removed at the last
  `cleanup`. `deinit` removes nothing from DNS (it is network I/O and cannot report): call `cleanup`
  first, `pendingCount` says what is left.
- **Propagation:** the zone's NS names → their addresses (`zone.nameserverIps`, resolved on every pass; a
  name whose lookup fails counts as "not yet" under `require_all_authoritative`, never as absent, and a
  name with no address at all is left out) → each server asked with RD clear; a server
  counts once one of its addresses answers with the value; an address that does not answer is
  skipped. Every server must agree unless `require_all_authoritative` is off; with
  `check_resolvers` the recursive resolvers must also answer with it. Polled every
  `propagation_interval_ms` until `propagation_timeout_ms`. The NS list and each name's address list come
  off the network, so the budget is checked before every query, not between passes (the first query is
  always made, so a zero timeout still asks once).
- **Publishers** keep their configuration and a static `note` (also reachable through `Publisher.note`, a function the four
  built-ins set: after a failed publish `Dns01Solver.note` is the publisher's own note, `the publisher failed` when it has
  none); `AcmeDns.Store` holds the accounts of several domains in go-acmedns' JSON file (`{"<domain>": {username, password,
  fulldomain, subdomain}}`; `register` makes and keeps one, `save` writes it atomically at mode 0600, `load` reads it, a
  missing file is an empty store, at most 1 MiB and 4096 accounts, passwords wiped when let go); `Rfc2136` adds the value (never
  replaces the RRset: a wildcard and its base validate at one name) and deletes exactly that value;
  `AcmeDns` refuses when the account's `fulldomain` is not where the CNAME leads (the usual setup
  error, which acme-dns itself would not report) and has no cleanup (acme-dns keeps the two newest
  values); `HttpReq` and `AcmeDns` never follow redirects (credentials ride along; a 3xx reply is named in `note` as "redirect not followed") and read the response
  body under the HTTP client's `total_timeout_ms` (64 KiB at most; so does `AcmeDns.register`); the
  endpoint's query string and fragment survive the path join; HttpReq's basic auth refuses a `:` in the
  user (RFC 7617) and credentials over 378 bytes ("user:password"), with their own note, encodes with
  `b64ct` and wipes the header buffer; `Exec` runs the program with a timeout in its own process group.

## Threat model / out of scope

The publishers authenticate to the DNS side with what the caller configures — a TSIG key, an
acme-dns API key, basic auth — and send it only to the configured endpoint (no redirects). The
`http` client's TLS verification applies to HTTPS endpoints; plain `http://` is the caller's
choice. The DNS answers this module reads (CNAME, SOA, NS, TXT) are unauthenticated: a spoofed
answer can only misdirect where the record is published or make the wait end early or late — the
CA validates on its own, so no certificate is issued on our word. `Exec` passes the record as
argv, never through a shell; in RAW mode that argv carries the key authorization, which any local
user can read in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` while the program runs (lego's RAW exec does the same). The
key authorization is the token plus the account key's thumbprint — public by the time the CA
validates, and no key material — so the exposure is a local observer learning the challenge early.
`AcmeDns.register`'s password (the account's API key) is wiped from the reply body before it is
freed and, through `AcmeDns.deinitRegistration`, from the result; a plain `Parsed.deinit` frees it
unwiped, and the `http` client's buffers are not wiped.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — published vectors, goldens captured from a foreign implementation, or a test run against a live foreign peer.

**What the tests actually contain.** In the module lane: the RFC 8555 §8.4 TXT value recomputed
independently of `acme.jws`, RFC 7617's basic-auth example, and the solver's bookkeeping without a
network. Live, `tools/interop.sh` (2026-10-16, 48 checks, 0 failures): Pebble v2.10.1 — Let's
Encrypt's test CA, a foreign black box — validates every DNS-01 challenge through a dnspython
authoritative server with RFC 2136 + TSIG (`modules/dns/tools/update_server.py`, the same server
`dns`'s own update interop runs against with BIND's `nsupdate` and `dig` as controls). One
certificate per publisher: RFC 2136 for a wildcard and its base (two values at one name), a CNAME
delegated into a second zone, an acme-dns account (registered, then delegated by CNAME), httpreq in
both modes, exec running BIND's `nsupdate`, `override_name` with `check_resolvers`, one of two
authoritative servers answering with `require_all_authoritative` off; and three that must fail
before the CA is asked (the same two servers with it on, a wrong TSIG secret reported as BADSIG, a
publisher that never publishes). After each: nothing pending, no TXT left behind. Also the zone
questions alone: SOA walk in both zones and for a name in neither, a cross-zone CNAME, a CNAME
loop, NS lookup. The Pebble flow's acme-dns side is a STAND-IN written from joohoi/acme-dns's README
(`tools/peer.py`); `tools/real_acmedns.sh` (2026-11-21) runs the real Go server (own DNS listener, own database) against
`AcmeDns`, its `Store` and `Dns01Solver`: register, three updates (the server keeps the two newest and its DNS answers
them), a wrong key and another account's subdomain refused with 401, the account file round trip, the solver end to end.

## What is deliberately not done

- **Vendor-API providers** (lego has 200+, libdns several dozen). The owner chose the four generic
  publishers (acme survey, Q2): a vendor API is a `Publisher` of the caller's own.
- **GSS-TSIG** for Windows "secure only" zones: none of the references has it (lego's `rfc2136`, certbot's
  `dns-rfc2136` and libdns' rfc2136 sign with TSIG HMAC keys, from their documentation) and it needs a Kerberos
  stack; `dns.tsig` is HMAC only.

## Verification

- **Run:** `scripts/modtest acmedns`; the live lane is `tools/interop.sh` under `hw run` (see `tools/README.md`).
- **Tests by area:** `solver_test.zig` — the solver's bookkeeping without a network (the record the publisher
  sees, the RFC 8555 §8.4 value recomputed independently of `acme.jws`, two values at one name, cleanup by
  domain and value, the options, the key-authorization wipe, an allocation-failure sweep over `present`);
  `zone_test.zig` — the CNAME and SOA walks, NS lookup and the propagation check against a scripted DNS
  server on loopback (bounds, wrong class / owner / type answers, partial address failures, the RD bit,
  allocation failures); `publishers_test.zig` — each publisher's wire (acme-dns and httpreq requests against a
  recording HTTP peer (and `AcmeDns.Store`: the file format, the 0600 write, hostile files, allocation failures), the RFC 2136 update against a UDP stub, `Exec` argv / exit / stderr / timeout against
  shell scripts); basic auth against RFC 7617's example (in `publishers.zig`); `hostile_test.zig` — a peer that sends its head and stalls.
- **Fuzz:** `fuzz_test.zig`, run by testkit's deterministic driver as `ACMEDNS_FUZZ`: the acme-dns `/register`
  reply, a TXT reply through `zone.txtPresent`, and the zone walks (`followCname`, `findZone`, `nameservers`,
  `nameserverIps`) against a scripted hostile DNS server on loopback (CNAME loops and a CNAME to the root, SOA/NS/A
  records of the wrong owner, class or type, junk rdata, error codes; one found defect: a CNAME to the root ended the walk
  at an empty name, now `error.ResolverFailed`), with reach checks in every test run (60 seeds for the walks, which cost
  a loopback server each).
- **Interop:** Pebble validates every DNS-01 challenge through a dnspython RFC 2136 + TSIG server, one
  certificate per publisher (see *Anchoring*).
- **Not observable here:** the system-resolver branch needs a controlled `/etc/resolv.conf` (the interop lane
  covers it); the key-authorization wipe is invisible to a spy in safe builds (its test bites in ReleaseFast).
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation run and the delta runs after it.
- **Delta mutation 2026-11-25:** 42 mutants over the publisher and store changes since 2026-11-14; 41 killed, 1 unobservable (the `fsync` before `rename` in `Store.save`: only a crash between the two shows it); six new tests in `src/publishers_test.zig`, two of them ReleaseFast-only.
